title: Asian Fashion Store: Korea, Thailand and Beyond, Chosen Piece by Piece
seo_title: Asian Fashion Store: Korea, Thailand | Oops, Mine Co.
meta_description: An asian fashion store with Korean, Thai and Vietnamese finds picked one at a time. Small batches, a wide color range, real measurements. Come and look twice.

hero.intro: One rail for everything we bring in from across Asia: Korea and Thailand first, with Vietnam and a few other countries in the mix. If you have been hunting for ladies asian fashion that is not already on every other boutique page, start here and look twice.

category.name: Asian Fashion
category.description: One place for everything we source across Asia — Korea and Thailand first, with Vietnam and other countries in the mix. Small runs, so the rail keeps changing.

sections.heading: What makes this asian fashion store different
paragraphs: Plenty of shops buy whatever a supplier has by the crate that month, price it low and hope. We do the slower version. Pieces come in one at a time from small makers and boutiques in Korea, Thailand and a few other countries, and only when something about them earns a second look — a sleeve that falls differently, a knit with real weight in the hand, a print you have not already met on ten other pages this week.

So the rail keeps moving. A style we love may arrive as a run of a dozen, sell through, and never come back in the same color. That is the honest trade of asian fashion for women who would rather not match the room: fewer of each piece, more pieces worth having, and no pretending a restock is on its way when it is not.
bullets: Picked piece by piece from small runs, never by the catalog page
Fabric first — weight, drape, and how it behaves after a wash
One detail you can point at: a cuff, a button, a print nobody else is showing
A wide color range, and as many sizes as each maker offers

sections.heading: Korea: clean lines, clever detail
paragraphs: Korea is where this range started and it is still the biggest part of it. The fit runs neat through the shoulder and easy everywhere else, so a plain knit reads polished with almost no effort from you. Look for cropped knits, midi skirts with some swing, denim cut differently from the usual US shape, and layering pieces that earn their place three seasons out of four. If you want the stage-inspired end of it — short pleats, cropped everything, sneakers with the lot — that sits in the K-pop edit.

sections.heading: Thailand: color you can feel across the room
paragraphs: Thailand brings the color. Light fabric for hot afternoons, prints with more going on in them than a plain floral, and hand-finished touches — an embroidered edge, a covered button, a tie that is properly sewn down rather than tacked on. Thai pieces travel well too: they pack small, come out of the bag looking fine, and read relaxed or dressed depending on the shoe you put with them. They sit happily beside the Korean pieces, which is how most of this rail gets worn — one from each, one outfit.

sections.heading: Vietnam, and an honest note about what we do not stock
paragraphs: Asian fashion is not one look, and we are not going to pretend we cover all of it. Korea and Thailand are the backbone. Vietnam comes in for linen, cotton and quiet, well-sewn basics, and other countries turn up when a piece earns the spot. What you will not find here is south asian fashion in the traditional sense — no saris, no lehengas, no salwar kameez. Those are their own trades and deserve a seller who knows them properly. Better we say so now than waste your afternoon.

sections.heading: Three ways to wear it this week
paragraphs: Almost nothing here asks for a whole new closet behind it. Your asian fashion style can read soft, sharp or a little playful off the same three pieces — the shoes decide which. Build any of these from one order and you have a week of outfits.
bullets: Weekday quiet — a Korean knit top, a midi skirt, flat sneakers, one good earring. Four minutes, done.
Dinner, no fuss — a printed Thai piece, a heeled sandal, hair up. Let the print talk and keep the jewelry small.
Travel day — wide-leg linen, a cropped knit over it, a bag you wear across you. Comes out of the suitcase ready.

sections.heading: Fit and sizing, before you add to cart
paragraphs: Sizing from Asia is not US sizing, and the gap is wide enough to matter. One maker's large can be the next one's medium, so we publish measurements — bust, waist, hip, length — on the product page instead of leaning on a letter. Take a piece you already wear and love, measure it flat, and match the numbers. That garment tells you more than any chart will.

Between two sizes, go with the one that suits your largest measurement: a knit can be belted, a shoulder seam cannot move. Where a style runs small, or the fabric has no give, the product page says so. The size guide covers the how-to-measure part, and if you are stuck between two, write to us from the contact page and you get a real opinion back. If it still is not right when it lands, the return policy sets out what happens next.

sections.heading: New pieces, small batches, and the words you typed
paragraphs: New pieces land in small batches through the season rather than on a fixed day of the month. They get shown on Facebook Live first, the email list hears next, and the site catches up. That is the only reason to move while a piece is still sitting there: runs are small, sizes go unevenly, and on a sold-out style the most we can honestly promise is to watch for something close. No countdown clocks, no invented "almost gone" banners.
Search boxes are not grammatical, and we do not mind. Here are plain answers to the phrases that bring people to this page.
bullets: "ladies asian fashion" — women's cuts only, in as many sizes as each small batch allows.
"is it really from Korea?" — the Korean pieces are sourced from Korea, the Thai ones from Thailand. Nothing gets relabeled on the way.
"do you have it in my size?" — sometimes. Sizes sell out at different speeds, so the product page is the honest answer, not this one.
"who picks all this?" — our owner does, style by style, which is why the rail has a point of view instead of a supplier list.

faqs.q: Is this asian fashion women can wear to work?
faqs.a: Most of it, yes. We buy for real weeks — desk, errands, dinner — not for one photo. Knits, midi skirts, easy trousers and simple dresses make up the bulk of the rail, and a louder print behaves under a plain cardigan. If your office leans formal, stay with the quieter colors and check the length and neckline listed on the product page before you order.

faqs.q: Where do your pieces come from?
faqs.a: Most of the asian fashion we carry comes from Korea and Thailand, with Vietnam close behind and other countries in the mix when a piece earns the spot. We buy from small makers and boutiques, one style at a time, which is why the rail changes so often. Oops, Mine Co. is an online boutique based in Houston, TX, and our owner chooses every piece herself.

faqs.q: Do you sell south asian fashion, like saris or lehengas?
faqs.a: No. Our range sits in East and Southeast Asia — Korea, Thailand, Vietnam and nearby. Saris, lehengas and salwar kameez are their own trades, and buying them well takes knowledge we do not have. What you will find here is the everyday side: knits, dresses, skirts, denim and separates you can wear on a Tuesday and again on Saturday.

As many as each maker offers on the style. Sizing from Asia tends to run smaller than US sizing, so we ask for the full run wherever it exists and list measurements on every product page. Compare those numbers with something already hanging in your closet rather than guessing from a letter — the size guide walks through how to measure and what to do when you are between two.

faqs.q: Will you restock a piece I missed?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and rarely in the same color. Runs are small and a lot of what we buy is one batch only. The quicker route is the email list: you hear when new pieces land, and that is usually where the closest match turns up. Tell us what you were after and we will keep an eye out for it while we are buying.

We are online only. The Houston, TX address on our contact page takes mail, not visitors, so there is no rail to flick through in person. What you get instead is the whole range in one place, Facebook Live for a closer look at fabric and fit, and an inbox you can write to before you buy. Ask us anything and you get a straight answer.

cta.heading: Find something yours
cta.text: Small batches, new faces, no restock promises. Leave your email and you will hear when something lands — the finds, not daily mail.
